result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers call the spec solid in their opening line. Both then bury that verdict under long lists of 'fix before Friday' items, labeled as blocking or as safety gaps, and neither clearly says it's fine to ship. A gives more specific credit to strengths, such as inline errors, tap targets and spacing, but it invents a problem by claiming the 520px width will break at 360px, which contradicts the spec's mobile testing. B avoids that mistake but nitpicks the 8px scale and gives less specific praise, so overall they come out about even. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers bury a positive verdict under a long list of must-fix items, which goes against the spirit of the rubric. A says 'The spec is solid' more cleanly and has fewer items overall. B lists 15 numbered issues, and one of them is manufactured: it claims the 520px width will force sideways scrolling, even though the spec says this was tested at 360px with no horizontal scroll. B does credit more specific strengths in its Keep section.
